summary: Gives a brief overview of the North American Directory Forum's Standing Document series. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: The North American Directory Forum planned a public directory service shared by competing providers. This memo summarizes the forum's numbered documents that describe how the service would work.

questions: what is the north american directory forum
what is the nadf public directory service
subtitle: An overview of the North American Directory Forum's X.500 standing documents.

tldr.problem: Competing service providers in the North American Directory Forum wanted to offer a cooperative public directory service using X.500.
tldr.mechanism: The forum's numbered Standing Documents describe its agreements on scope, service, naming, operations, security, and accounting.
tldr.outcome: This Informational memo summarizes the documents and their availability; it obsoletes RFC 1417, RFC 1295, RFC 1255, and RFC 1218.

today: RFC 1758 is Informational and obsoletes RFC 1417. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Forum and Its Document Series
sections.content:
The North American Directory Forum (NADF) is a group of service providers planning to cooperatively offer a Public Directory Service in North America using the CCITT X.500 Recommendations.

RFC 1758 gives an overview of Standing Documents SD-0 through SD-13. The documents describe agreements needed for a cooperative service offered by competing providers, relying on X.500(88) where possible.
sections.plainLanguage: The NADF brought service providers together to plan a shared public directory. Its numbered documents recorded the agreements for that service.

sections.title: Directory Structure and Naming
sections.content:
SD-5 describes a national Directory Information Tree subtree and applies its approach to c=CA and c=US. It distinguishes a public name-space for publicly recognized entities from private name-spaces managed by individual directory providers.

SD-6 gives guidance for private name-spaces. SD-7 covers mapping the tree to multiple Directory Management Domains, and SD-12 lists ADDMD names.
sections.plainLanguage: The naming documents describe public and provider-managed parts of the directory. Other documents explain how those parts connect across management domains.

sections.title: Service, Security, and Administration
sections.content:
SD-3 covers service agreements such as quality of service, and SD-4 covers the directory schema. SD-8 describes the NADF pilot, while SD-9 covers the central administration's charter, procedures, and operations.

SD-10 addresses security and privacy policy, SD-11 describes directory security mechanisms, and SD-13 gives accounting and settlement principles.
sections.plainLanguage: The remaining documents cover service quality, the directory's structure, a pilot, administration, security, privacy, and payments among providers.

sections.title: Availability of the Documents
sections.content:
The standing documents were available in hardcopy and PostScript form. Because they did not exist in ASCII form, they could not be distributed as Informational RFCs.

The memo lists the NADF Secretariat for hardcopy requests and an anonymous FTP location for PostScript files. Its security section says security issues are not discussed.
sections.plainLanguage: The source documents were available in print and PostScript, not ASCII. This memo itself does not discuss security issues.
